head_commit.message:
docs(record): log owner decision D13 — the paper keeps the published-test scorecard

D13 (owner answer 2026-11-08, option a): no paper change. The paper's channel
counts stay the published-sigma_unc tallies of section A.15 (1 PASS / 0 MARGINAL /
7 FAIL at the canonical Phase-44 parameters; 5 PASS / 2 MARGINAL / 1 FAIL at the
v19.2-E A.2 5-parameter DE best fit). The adopted T120 arm tally (7 PASS /
1 MARGINAL / 0 FAIL at a_slope 0.5 and 0.8) stays repo-internal.

Reason recorded: the T120 scoreboard scores eight project-stated bounds, not the
A.15 channel slots; drift_guard already states the tallies must not be compared;
one of its seven passes (Cloud-9) is judged against the 100 cm2/g floor that F21
showed to be this project's own model output, so a '7 of 8' headline belongs to
the overclaim class of the retracted R88(67) '8/8 channels pass'. The implicit
drift risk (paper describes the canonical arm, CURRENT.md records adopted arms)
is written down rather than left to be rediscovered.

Recorded in three places: CURRENT.md D13 paragraph, INTEGRITY_FINDINGS owner
decisions table D13 row, CHANGELOG [ScorecardDecision-D13-2026-11-08]. The cg16
host-path inventory was regenerated by scripts/cg16_scan.py because docs prose
changed; its guard test went red first, as designed, then passed 7/7.

No paper, code, fit or PDF change. Re-verified after the edits: drift_guard no
drift, t82 120/120 ALL CLEAR, audit_claims PASS, check_fabrication OK,
audit_doc_anchors PASS, audit_stale_strings PASS, audit_register_state PASSED,
audit_units clean, doc guards 20 passed.

head_commit.message:
fix(evidence): store the gate logs as .txt so they are actually tracked

.gitignore line 78 ignores *.log, so the gate and audit logs copied into this evidence folder in the two
previous commits were on disk but not in the repository - those commit messages overstated what landed.
Followed the existing convention from evidence_n24/_n25/_n26 (gate_run_committed.txt, gate_run_final.txt,
gate_run_failed_*.txt): both passing gates (efd6021 and 4a2ffdc, 15/15), the standalone render audit, and
both failed pre-fix runs are now tracked. README records the ignore rule so the next round does not repeat
the mistake.
